title: AWS Agent-EvalKit Developer Tutorial 2026
overview: Agent-EvalKit is an open-source toolkit (Apache 2.0) released by AWS on June 11, 2026 that automates AI agent evaluation directly inside developer environments via AI coding assistants. It integrates with Claude Code, Kiro CLI, and Kilo Code, bringing structured evaluation into the development workflow rather than treating it as a post-deployment activity.
keyHighlights: Integrates with Claude Code, Kiro CLI, Kilo Code
Six-phase evaluation workflow: Plan, Data, Trace, Run Agent, Eval, Report
Combines code-based evaluators with LLM-as-judge scoring
Uses OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing for agent instrumentation
Generates code-level improvement recommendations with file references
Requires Amazon Bedrock for LLM-as-judge scoring phase
Supports Strands Agents SDK, LangGraph, and CrewAI for auto-instrumentation
Installed via `uv tool install evalkit` from GitHub

sixEvaluationPhases.description: Analyzes agent source code (tool definitions, system prompt, framework config) and designs an evaluation strategy with targeted metrics
Generates test cases for evaluation, including edge cases (empty results, wrong params, insufficient permissions, stale data)
sixEvaluationPhases.artifact: Test cases with ground truth outcomes

sixEvaluationPhases.description: Instruments agent with OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing to capture tool calls, model responses, and intermediate state
Executes the agent against each test case while collecting structured traces
Implements metrics from the plan as executable evaluation code (supports DeepEval, Strands Evals SDK), runs against traces, saves structured results
Analyzes patterns across test cases and generates fix recommendations referencing specific files, behaviors, and expected impact

cliCommands.description: Guided step-by-step evaluation (recommended for first-time users)
Analyze agent and design evaluation strategy

quickStartSteps: 2. Install EvalKit: uv tool install evalkit --from git+https://github.com/awslabs/Agent-EvalKit.git
3. Initialize project: evalkit init my-agent-evaluation && cd my-agent-evaluation
4. Copy agent code into project: cp -r /path/to/agent-folder .
5. Start AI assistant: claude (or kiro, kilocode)
6. Run guided eval: /evalkit.quick Evaluate my agent at ./agent-folder for response quality and tool accuracy

caseStudy.title: Travel Research Agent (Strands Agents SDK + Amazon Bedrock)
caseStudy.keyFinding: Agent scored 83.9% on response quality but only 32.3% on faithfulness — a critical gap caused by hallucination on empty tool results that standard output-level testing failed to catch

risks: Evaluation pipeline manipulation could corrupt agent quality signals
Source code exfiltration via evaluation context window
LLM01 (Prompt Injection) and LLM05 (Supply Chain Vulnerabilities) are primary OWASP mappings
Evaluation test case datasets should be treated as trusted inputs with integrity controls
mitigations: Apply write-access controls and integrity verification to evaluation dataset files
Sanitize tool return values before passing to LLM judge prompts
Restrict AI coding assistant network access during evaluation runs
Pin Agent-EvalKit and dependency tree in CI/CD
Separate evaluation pipeline credentials from production agent credentials

relatedAwsServices.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
relatedAwsServices.description: Managed AWS service for agent evaluation with built-in evaluators (Helpfulness, Faithfulness, Goal Success), custom code-based evaluators via Lambda, and online/on-demand/batch modes
relatedAwsServices.keyDifference: AgentCore is a managed service; Agent-EvalKit is an open-source CLI toolkit that runs locally via AI coding assistants

relatedAwsServices.name: awslabs/agent-evaluation
relatedAwsServices.description: Earlier open-source framework (2024) for testing virtual agents via LLM orchestrator, using multi-turn conversations; predecessor lineage to Agent-EvalKit

competitorComparison.langfuse: Closed-source LLM observability platform; Agent-EvalKit is open-source and dev-environment-integrated
competitorComparison.promptfoo: Open-source eval framework focused on prompt testing; Agent-EvalKit is agent-specific with code-reading capability
competitorComparison.deepeval: Open-source LLM evaluation framework; Agent-EvalKit supports DeepEval as a backend but adds the full six-phase workflow
competitorComparison.braintrust: Enterprise AI evaluation platform; Agent-EvalKit is free, open-source, and tightly coupled with AI coding assistants
